source_name: NCR Atleos corporate site (banking / ATM-as-a-Service / managed services)
why_relevant: Post-split NCR entity that owns the ATM hardware, ATM-as-a-Service and ATM managed-services business; self-describes as the largest ATM deployer globally with ~7,000 customer engineers in 60 countries. NCR is confirmed present in the Slovenian installed base (serviced locally by Demi Trade; also historically supplied through Printec). The site's banking, ATM-management and ATMaaS pages plus its newsroom are the primary place any Slovenian win, partner appointment or service-model shift would surface.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf corporate site and EMEA global-locations directory
source_subtype: OEM vendor corporate site + locations directory + newsroom
why_relevant: Diebold Nixdorf is a confirmed brand in the Slovenian ATM installed base (locally serviced by Demi Trade). Its global-locations directory is the canonical way to establish whether it covers Slovenia via a legal entity, a neighbouring-country hub (Austria/Croatia/Slovakia) or a partner - a decisive fact for how it competes here. Note: the EMEA/Slovakia locations URL returned a 404-titled result in search, so the directory structure appears to have moved and needs re-derivation from the site nav rather than being recorded as dead.

source_name: KEBA banking automation - references and news
source_subtype: OEM vendor references page + news feed
why_relevant: Austrian cash-recycling specialist and a natural competitor in Slovenia given the Austrian banking groups active here (Sparkasse/Erste, Addiko, BKS, Raiffeisen lineage). KEBA maintains an explicit customer references page and a banking-automation news feed that names individual bank deployments (e.g. an Erste/Sparkasse self-service branch with KePlus FT10, outdoor recyclers for Sparkasse Dornbirn) - the reference page is the highest-yield way to detect a Slovenian or Slovenian-parent-group win. Its evo-series product pages define the recycler feature set competitors are benchmarked against.

source_name: Auriga SpA - omnichannel/ATM software (incl. ACI partner listing)
source_subtype: ISV vendor site + third-party partner directory entry
why_relevant: Auriga is the leading independent multivendor ATM/branch-automation software competitor (WWS platform), the software half of this cell where hardware is commoditised. Its ACI Worldwide partner page documents the WWS + ACI Enterprise Payments combination for NextGen ATM and self-service banking, video-assisted terminals and QR/mobile-enabled ATM functions - i.e. the exact stack a Slovenian bank would evaluate against an incumbent's own software. Vendor + partner-ecosystem pages are where a Slovenian reference would first appear.

source_name: CIMA S.p.A. - cash automation / under-counter safes (via Slovenian distributor Demi Trade)
source_subtype: OEM vendor site + distributor network page
why_relevant: CIMA is confirmed present in Slovenia through Demi Trade, which distributes CIMA automatic under-counter cash safes - the only hard, evidence-backed Slovenian channel link found for CIMA in this pass. Branch teller-cash automation (TCR/under-counter recyclers) is the branch-automation adjacency of this cell and a direct competitive overlap. The OEM site's distributor/contacts section should confirm the Slovenian representation formally.

source_name: Podnadzorom / Varnost Grdadolnik - bancna oprema
why_relevant: Slovenian security-systems integrator with a dedicated bank-equipment product line. Security integrators are a recurring adjacent channel for ATM safes, deposit units, branch physical security and increasingly for self-service enclosures, so this maps another local competitor/partner class that pure vendor-page searches miss.

source_name: Printec Slovenija (incumbent country site - channel benchmark)
why_relevant: The incumbent's own Slovenian country site. Included not as a competitor but as the reference baseline for how this channel presents itself locally (30+ years, 900 employees, 500 customers, 16 countries, 23,000 ATMs, 650,000 POS) and because its Slovenian case history is documented publicly - it supplied NCR bank ATMs and co-delivered the automatic cash-deposit service with Bankart and Abanka Vipa. Competitor country pages should be diffed against this page's structure (offer, references, smart safe) to make comparisons like-for-like.

source_name: Banka Slovenije - statistika placil / payment statistics and reporting rules
source_subtype: central bank statistics + regulatory reporting framework
why_relevant: The regulator publishes the authoritative Slovenian ATM and POS terminal counts and mandates that ATM network operators report payment statistics - the official denominator for any market-share claim in this cell. Observed figures: ATMs fell 1.9% to 1,284 at end-H2 2024 with ~74% contactless-capable, while POS terminals grew ~11% YoY to ~47,000. A shrinking-but-upgrading ATM estate is precisely the replacement-cycle signal that drives cash-recycler and branch-automation tenders. The reporting-obligation page also identifies who counts as an ATM network operator - a de facto register of market participants.

source_name: Ministrstvo za finance - predlog zakona o placilnih sredstvih / dostopnost gotovine (public consultation)
why_relevant: The single strongest forward-looking demand driver for this cell. The draft act on payment instruments, in public consultation as of this run, would oblige credit institutions and Posta Slovenije to maintain a sufficient network of cash points, require an ATM within 5 km of the centre of any settlement over 1,000 inhabitants, and let Banka Slovenije order a named bank to install an ATM or open a branch in an under-served area. If enacted (government reading expected September, possible adoption before year-end), it mechanically creates new ATM placements in a market that has been shrinking - a direct pipeline signal for every vendor in this cell. Consultation drafts also attract bank and association comments naming cost and equipment constraints.

source_name: AJPES - Poslovni register Slovenije and eObjave
why_relevant: The official register of all Slovenian business entities plus the eObjave publication service. This is how you (a) confirm whether NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Glory, Auriga or KEBA have a registered Slovenian legal entity or branch versus serving via a foreign hub or local agent, and (b) pull filed annual accounts for local competitors like Demi Trade to size their service revenue. Registry search by activity code also surfaces competitors that never rank in web search.

source_name: Slovenian bank ATM/branch locators (NLB, UniCredit, OTP, Delavska hranilnica, DBS, Sparkasse, Addiko, BKS)
why_relevant: Each bank publishes its own ATM and branch locator, and critically flags which units accept deposits ('polog') - Delavska hranilnica marks deposit-capable ATMs explicitly, UniCredit and OTP publish per-unit capability. Diffing these locators over time reveals deposit/recycling function rollouts unit by unit, which is the closest public proxy for cash-recycler purchases. NLB's Bank&Go mobile branch is a further self-service/branch-automation format worth tracking as a competing service model.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Slovenia branch-renovation / self-service microsites
why_relevant: Banks publish per-branch renovation microsites when they convert a branch to a new self-service format. These pages describe the new equipment and customer journey and are the closest thing to a public branch-automation case study in Slovenia - useful for inferring which vendor's format (recycler, video teller, assisted self-service kiosk) was chosen, and for benchmarking the pace of branch-automation conversion across the network.

source_name: ATM Marketplace and ATMIA vendor showrooms
why_relevant: Trade-press aggregator plus the ATM Industry Association showroom directory. Both maintain per-vendor company showcases (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf and peers) that consolidate product lines, press releases and partner/deployment announcements in one place, and ATMIA membership/showroom listings are an efficient way to snowball the full competitor set in this cell - including smaller OEMs and regional integrators that never appear in Slovenian-language search.

source_name: Slovenian general and business news on ATM fleet economics (Delo, 24ur, Svet24, Siol, Necenzurirano, Forbes Slovenija, Cekin)
why_relevant: Mainstream Slovenian outlets are where ATM-fleet economics actually become public: Euronet's arrival and its move to start charging withdrawal fees, the shrinking-network debate, the cash-access bill's ATM coverage mandates, and the launch of instant automatic cash deposit at ATMs. These stories routinely name operators, functions and sometimes suppliers, and they date events - which is what turns vendor claims into a verifiable timeline.

source_name: Slo-Tech forum - ATM and self-service threads
why_relevant: Slovenia's main technical community forum, with long-running threads on automatic cash deposit at ATMs and on Euronet's entry into the Slovenian market. Reveals-indirectly source: technically literate posters identify machine makes and models, report which branches got which equipment, and surface complaints about deposit reliability - ground-truth detail no vendor or bank publishes. Low individual credibility, high value as a lead generator to verify elsewhere.

source_name: Hrc — Aktualno / novice (case studies: Hibis migrations)
why_relevant: News index carrying project-level case studies that name the bank and the migration: Deželna banka Slovenije migration to Hibis, Hibis as the common platform of the merged OTP banka, and the Nova KBM Hibis implementation. This is exactly the deal-level evidence that the banks themselves never publish.

source_name: Halcom d.d. — corporate site (digital banking solutions)
why_relevant: The best-known Slovenian banking-software exporter (Hal E-Bank, MultiPay, qualified digital certificates, payment hub). Corporate site states market scale (5 markets, ~50 banks, 2 central banks/clearing houses, 700k+ certificates) and carries a dedicated 'For banks and financial institutions' offering page — the base layer for tracking Halcom's product line and positioning.

source_name: Halcom support — 'Banks in Slovenia' / 'List of banks that are using Halcom'
why_relevant: A vendor support FAQ that effectively publishes Halcom's installed base: which banks in Slovenia (and in other markets) support Hal E-Bank / Halcom certificates. Support-portal FAQs are usually maintained more honestly and more currently than marketing reference pages, so this is a high-value customer-list proxy.

source_name: ZZI d.o.o. — bizBox / eCustoms corporate site
why_relevant: ZZI runs bizBox, a Slovenian e-document exchange network integrated with 68+ ERP/accounting systems and connected to banks and UJP for e-invoice exchange. Reveals the bank-side e-invoicing/e-document rails and which banks participate — an adjacency to payments that foreign vendors compete for.

source_name: SAOP help — 'Nastavitve za povezavo na ZZI: izmenjava e-računov z bankami in UJP'
why_relevant: Third-party ERP vendor documentation that confirms the ZZI–bank e-invoice integration path in operational detail. ERP/accounting help portals are a reliable indirect way to learn which banks expose which channels, because they must document real, working connections.

source_name: SRC d.o.o. — Rešitve za bančništvo in finance
why_relevant: SRC is one of the largest Slovenian system integrators with an explicit banking & finance solutions vertical (e-signature, digital identification, secure e-archive, customer-file / document management, regulatory compliance). It is a prime candidate for localising foreign platforms into SI banks, so its solution pages hint at the underlying foreign products.

source_name: Comtrade programske rešitve / Comtrade SI Sistemske integracije (Slovenia units)
why_relevant: Comtrade's Slovenian legal entities (Letališka cesta 29B, Ljubljana) are a major regional software/system-integration supplier with financial-sector work. The bizi.si company records give the exact entity names, activity codes and banking relationships needed to then query procurement and reference databases correctly — the Slovenian group site itself surfaced poorly in search.

source_name: si.openprocurements.com — supplier and buyer pages (Slovenian public procurement)
why_relevant: Aggregated Slovenian public-procurement data with per-supplier pages (e.g. Comtrade SI Sistemske integracije, Comtrade programske rešitve) and per-buyer pages including Banka Slovenije. Because Banka Slovenije and state-owned financial bodies must tender publicly, this is the single best route from a domestic IT house to a named contract, value and date — the deal evidence commercial banks withhold.

source_name: Špica International — corporate site (time & attendance, access control, supply chain)
why_relevant: Leading SI supplier of workforce time-tracking and physical access control (Kadris / Time&Space, All Hours). Relevant to banks as a facilities/HR-systems supplier rather than a core-banking one — note that Banka Slovenije has publicly tendered maintenance and upgrade of a Kadris 4 access-control and time-registration system, which is a concrete bank-side footprint for this class of vendor.

source_name: Genis d.o.o. — e-GenDoc document management
why_relevant: Domestic document-management/e-archive vendor (e-GenDoc, ISO 9001/27001-aligned). Banks are heavy buyers of certified DMS and legally-compliant e-archiving in Slovenia; Genis' news and solution pages are where such bank deployments surface. Its management also comments publicly on the crowded Slovenian DMS market, useful for competitor mapping.

source_name: Mikrografija d.o.o. — References / mSolutions / mIA
why_relevant: Has an explicit public References page plus product pages (mIA intelligent digital archiving, mSolutions). Certified digital archiving is a regulated purchase for SI banks, so a named reference list here converts directly into vendor–bank relationships. Bilingual (mikrografija.si in Slovenian, .com in English) so both language tracks are collectable.

source_name: Agitavit Solutions d.o.o. (Ljubljana) — company record and site
why_relevant: Mid-size Slovenian custom-software house (~97 employees, Letališka cesta 33F) active in finance/insurance business applications. Registry record establishes the entity for procurement and reference tracking; its own site is the follow-on target for banking/insurance case studies. Included as an actor-map entry for the cell.
